messages.subject: Trend estimation:  unmarkedFrameGMM and gmultmix?
parts:
I’ve been asked to analyze a data set that consists of 6 years’ single-
observer auditory point counts (N’s) for a single bird species, with 3
repeat visits to each of 166 points each year. The survey points were
arranged basically as a grid with distances between points sufficient
to make hearing the same individual from two points unlikely during
any particular round of visits. The assumption that the population is
closed within a year is considered acceptable. Interest is in
summarizing trends in the species’ abundance over the years, as well
as effects of other site and observation covariates besides year.

I’m aware that Kéry et al (Journal of Applied Ecology 2009, 46, 1163–
1172) urge Bayesian methods for such data, but they acknowledge that a
maximum likelihood approach may also have some appeal, and I’d like to
explore that if possible.

I’ve gotten the impression that unmarkedFrameGMM and gmultmix might be
applicable, but I haven’t found an example of those functions where
they are used with such data. I’ve tried to set up a gmultmix
analysis, but feel unconfident about what I’ve done, especially with
respect to obsToY and piFun.

These lines seem to work OK to set up an unmarkedFrameGMM without any
yearly site covariates:
o2y <- diag(18)
o2y[upper.tri(o2y)] <- 1
o2y

pmat <- matrix(1, nrow=18, ncol=18)

instPiFun <- function(p) {
M <- nrow(p)
J <- ncol(p)
pi <- matrix(NA, M, J)
for(i in 1:J) {
pi[,i] <- p[,i]
}
return(pi)
}
instPiFun(pmat)

umfGMM <-
unmarkedFrameGMM(data0308.y,siteCovs=covartemp2,obsCovs=obsCVGMM,
numPrimary=6,obsToY=o2y,piFun="instPiFun")

(The columns of counts and observation covariates are in sequential
order, year 1 = cols 1:3, year 2 = cols 4:6, etc. Also, there are a
few scattered NA’s among the counts and observation covariates, when
counts weren’t obtained.)

Then I add two yearly site covariates (here I treat ‘year’ as
continuous, but could alternatively treat it as a factor):

yearlySiteCovs(umfGMM) <- list(data.frame(rnyr =
rep(rainyr,numSites(umfGMM))),data.frame(year = (rep(1:6,
numSites(umfGMM)))))

Sorry for this long post, but I was hoping to get some some feedback
on whether this approach makes sense in general. I'd be happy to
provide more details on the data if that will help. If I’m “barking
up the wrong tree” altogether with gmultmix on data with such a
design, please let me know. If (switching metaphors) I’m in the
“right ballpark,” suggestions on the right piFun would be especially
appreciated. Again, thanks in advance for any comments on this.

RK

Hmmmm, I could be way out of your ballbark, but I think you may not have the necessary removal data or otherwise to estimate an availability parameter in a multinomial model. Makes me think the N-mixture model (pcount function) is more appropriate for your data but I may be wrong.

Matt

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Trend estimation: unmarkedFrameGMM and gmultmix?
parts:
Hi RK,

I may have released gmultmix too soon because there is no published paper to describe it. However, we hope to submit one soon. Although the model has broad applicability, it's probably best to think of it as a "single season" type of model in which the probability of an individual being available for detection (phi) is < 1, and the probability of detection given availability (p) is < 1. This allows one to relax the closure assumption, but it is not meant to estimate trends over multiple seasons per se. The model that I think you want was just published in Biometrics by Dail and Madsen (online only). We hope to include this in unmarked sometime soon, but it's not ready yet. In the meantime, you could try to adapt their R code, or you could use pcount to either analyze each year separately or model year as a fixed effect.

Back to gmultmix. Matt's comment is correct; gmultmix assumes a multinomial observation process, not a binomial process as would be the case with repeated counts nested within repeated counts. The binomial observation model may eventually be added.

users only need to specify "obsToY" and "piFun" when using multinomPois or gmultmix with data from a "non-standard" survey design, ie not with data from constant-interval removal sampling or double observer sampling. I will try to add more documentation regarding obsToY and piFun in the next release.

Hope this helps,
Richard

Thanks much for your replies Matt and Richard. I'm set to run pcount
on the years separately as you suggest, and also jointly, treating
each year's data at a site as if independent from other years' data at
a site. The latter is pseudoreplicative, but still may be useful for
some exploration. The obstacle that I need to get around is that if
all 18 counts for each site are presented to pcount in one row, then
'year' has to be treated as an observation covariate, and (unless I'm
misunderstanding) observation covariates can't be included in the

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Trend estimation: unmarkedFrameGMM and gmultmix?
parts:
If you want to analyze all years together with pcount, you could stack each year's data on top of each other and create a column to distinguish the years. Your response matrix would be RYxJ where R is the number of sites, Y is the number of years and J is the number of reps/year. You could test for interactions among year and each of your site covariates to determine if relationships differed among years. This is pretty much like analyzing each year separately, but your SE might be too small as you suggested.

fyi, the Dail and Madsen paper has an online appendix with some R code.

Thanks for your positive feedback.

Richard
